S1.name: Structured data reasoning
S1.description: Reasoning over structured product or flight attributes (price, size, material, capacity, zoom, etc.) to select the correct variant from a catalog. Dominant in retail where agents must match complex product specifications.

S2.name: Tool calling precision
S2.description: Calling tools with incorrect arguments: wrong item IDs, wrong passenger names, wrong flight numbers, wrong payment amounts. The most widespread failure type across both domains.

S3.name: Multi-step completion
S3.description: Failure to complete all required actions in a multi-step task. Includes partial completions, skipped steps, and hitting max_steps. The single most common failure mode overall.

S4.name: Precondition verification
S4.description: Performing actions (cancellation, modification, refund) without verifying that policy preconditions are met. Very prevalent in airline domain where many policy restrictions exist.

S5.name: Numerical reasoning
S5.description: Errors in arithmetic: wrong certificate amounts, wrong price differences, wrong payment splits, wrong refund totals. Common in both domains.

S6.name: Record discovery
S6.description: Failure to find or look up the relevant records (flights, orders, user details, addresses) needed to complete the task. Includes failing to search when the user does not provide an ID.

S7.name: Information communication
S7.description: DB state correct but agent failed to communicate required information (totals, refund amounts, IDs) to the user. Relatively rare but clear when it occurs.

S8.name: Conditional/state reasoning
S8.description: Failure to follow conditional instructions ('if X then do Y, else Z') or to track mid-conversation state changes. Prominent in retail tasks with complex user decision trees.

S9.name: Language fluency
S9.description: Potential misinterpretation of non-native English speaker's request. Very limited evidence.

S11.name: Tone/empathy
S11.description: Agent capitulated to social pressure (flattery, emotional appeals, anger) and either violated policy or failed to complete tasks. Includes being derailed into off-topic roleplay.

S13.name: Format compliance
S13.description: No clear evidence of format compliance failures in this run.

S14.name: Context window management
S14.description: Conversations that produced empty responses or lost track of complex multi-part requests, suggesting context overflow or state loss.

skill_summary.notes: S10 (response latency), S12 (hallucination of tools), S15 (multilingual), and S16 (proactive upselling) showed no clear evidence of being primary failure causes in this run.
